claim_verdicts.evidence: Kanban Guide (R1 WebFetch): start work on an item (pull or select) 'only when there is a clear signal that there is capacity to do so'; no sprints or time-boxes prescribed. Repo lines 3-4: 'Đội không chia sprint ... việc vào bảng bất cứ lúc nào, xếp theo mức ưu tiên'. Lesson sec 4/6 and q3 option a ('someone can take it and Đang làm has room') now match 'capacity'.

Scrum Guide 2020 (WebFetch R3): 'The Scrum Guide contains the definition of Scrum.' Sprints: 'They are fixed length events of one month or less to create consistency.' 'No changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal.' Search found no mention of boards, columns or Kanban (negative result from a processed summary). 'short official description' is an acceptable L1 gloss of 'the definition of Scrum'.

git show stage-1:docs/team/kanban-board-example.md: lines 8-12 and 24-28 match both code blocks character-for-character. Line 14 heading 'Vì sao "Đang làm" giới hạn hai việc'; lines 16-20: column already has two items, 'giới hạn nghĩa là dừng ... Một cột đầy là tín hiệu tắc nghẽn'. Lines 24-26: support team no sprint, feature team keeps sprints. Reading the same label on Chờ review as 'at most two' is the plain meaning.
git show stage-1:docs/team/sprint-example.md line 17: '| Ngừng gửi thông báo cho đơn đã hủy | Dev 3 | 2 | Chưa xong, chuyển sprint sau |'.

Scrum Guide 2020: 'The Sprint Backlog is composed of the Sprint Goal (why), the set of Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint (what), as well as an actionable plan' - per Sprint. Kanban Guide (R1): Kanban 'can and should be used to augment' other techniques. Lesson now says 'Teams can mix them' (sec 4, summary 5), matching the claim; no prevalence statement remains.

Scrum Guide 2020: 'Sprint Planning initiates the Sprint by laying out the work to be performed for the Sprint.' 'The Developers select items from the Product Backlog to include in the current Sprint.' Events: Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective. R3 zero issues; opened: scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html (WebFetch), kanbanguides.org (R1), git show stage-1 of kanban-board-example.md and sprint-example.md, track.yaml outline.

issues.text: Round 2. 'daily' and 'retrospective' I know from the prereq, but 'review' as a meeting I do not; the board's 'Waiting for review' column uses 'review' for code review, so I briefly wonder if this is the same thing. Not needed for the main idea.
issues.quote: keeping Scrum's roles and meetings (daily, review, retrospective)
issues.fix: Replace '(daily, review, retrospective)' with '(such as the daily and the retrospective)'.

issues.text: Round-1 Dev 3 issue, now smaller: Try it no longer asks for names, but the prose points at names ('with the developer's name') and the second block says the support team is Dev 1, Dev 2 and the feature team Dev 3, Dev 4, while the support board shows Dev 3. I still pause, though nothing in the exercise or quiz depends on it.
issues.quote: Sửa lỗi trang sản phẩm bị chậm — Dev 3
issues.fix: Propose a repo change (prompt 08) so that board item belongs to Dev 1 or Dev 2; until then, drop 'with the developer's name once someone works on it' so the prose does not draw attention to the names.

issues.text: Unchanged from round 1: 'Postgres' in a board item is unknown to me. It is only a task label, not needed for the idea.
issues.fix: No change needed; optionally add '(the database)' if the prose ever mentions that item.

issues.text: Unchanged from round 1: I re-read this sentence twice; 'defaults for when work moves' and 'rival beliefs' are abstract, and the next sentence says it plainly.
issues.quote: The two are different defaults for when work moves, not rival beliefs.
issues.fix: Replace with 'The two differ in when work moves; neither is the right one for every team.'

issues.text: Across the quiz the correct option is the longest in every question (q1 b, q2 c, q3 a, q4 a, q5 a). In q1 and q3 I can answer from the text, but a reader who notices the pattern can pick without reading. q1 b is no longer verbatim (round-1 point resolved).
issues.quote: A time box of fixed length with one goal
issues.fix: In at least two questions, lengthen one wrong option to match the correct one, e.g. q1 d: 'Priorities that say which item should be picked up next'.

issues.text: Stem is clear now (no 'sprint backlog'). Still guessable: b ('not allowed to use boards') and d ('exactly four columns') are absurd, and c is the only long, reasoned option.
issues.quote: False, because it still works in two-week sprints with a goal; the board alone is not Kanban.
issues.fix: Make d plausible, e.g. 'False, because Kanban boards never have a Done column'.

issues.text: Unchanged: guessable by elimination; c and d are obviously silly, and a is the longest option and repeats the context's wording.
issues.quote: Its work arrives unpredictably and some cannot wait, which suits flow better than a planned batch
issues.fix: Replace c or d with a plausible wrong reason, e.g. 'Kanban boards show more columns, so the manager sees more detail'.

issues.text: Unchanged: a is the longest option and the only one about flow; b and c name things the lesson never mentions (manager every evening, only finished work).
issues.quote: Because items stay on it and move on as they progress, instead of being reset each sprint
issues.fix: Make one distractor plausible, e.g. 'Because Kanban items have no owner written on them'.
